questions.question:
The Service `nginx-external` in the namespace `exposure-lab` is exposed outside the cluster, but it must only be reachable from inside the cluster.

Change the Service accordingly. The Deployment `nginx` must keep being served through the Service (same name, same port 80).

verification.description: Service nginx-external is ClusterIP only: no node port, no external address
The Service still answers HTTP on port 80 inside the cluster

questions.question:
The user `jacob` has too many permissions in the namespace `dev-z`. To see the current (bad) state:

`kubectl auth can-i delete pods -n dev-z --as=jacob`

Jacob must only have these permissions in `dev-z`:

- `get`, `list` and `watch` on pods;
- `get` and `list` on configmaps;
- no access at all to secrets.

Update the permissions. You can edit the existing Role `dev-user-access`.

verification.description: jacob can get, list and watch pods and nothing more on pods
jacob can get and list configmaps and nothing more
jacob has no access to secrets and nothing besides pods and configmaps

questions.question:
Ensure that the kubelet of the worker node `{{NODE02}}` (`ssh {{NODE02}}`):

- **disables anonymous authentication**;
- **delegates the authorization decisions to the API server** (Webhook).

The change must survive a restart of the kubelet, and `{{NODE02}}` must stay `Ready`.

verification.description: The kubelet of {{NODE02}} rejects anonymous requests (anonymous.enabled=false, HTTP 401)
The kubelet of {{NODE02}} uses authorization.mode=Webhook
The kubelet configuration file keeps the settings and {{NODE02}} is Ready

questions.question:
The Pod `kiwi` in the namespace `sbom-lab` runs an old nginx image. Use `trivy` (available on this machine) to work with the Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) of that image. Save the files in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-007-q4/`:

1. Generate an **SPDX-JSON** SBOM of the image of the Pod and save it as `sbom.spdx.json`.
2. Generate a **CycloneDX** SBOM of the same image and save it as `sbom.cdx.json`.
3. Find in the SPDX SBOM the version of the package `openssl` and write it to `openssl-version.txt`.

verification.description: sbom.spdx.json is an SPDX-JSON SBOM of the image of the Pod kiwi
sbom.cdx.json is a CycloneDX SBOM of the image of the Pod kiwi
openssl-version.txt holds the version of the package openssl from the SBOM

questions.question:
In the namespace `rocket` the Deployment and the Service `rocket-server` (port 80) exist. A certificate and its key for the host `rocket-server.local` are in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-007-q5/` (`rocket.crt`, `rocket.key`).

The Traefik ingress controller (IngressClass `traefik`) is installed in the cluster, together with its CRDs (for example `Middleware`).

1. Create the TLS Secret `secret-tls` in `rocket` from the provided certificate and key.
2. Create the Ingress `rocket-ingress` in `rocket`: class `traefik`, host `rocket-server.local`, path `/` (type Prefix), backend Service `rocket-server` on port 80, TLS with the Secret `secret-tls`.
3. All HTTP traffic for the host must be **redirected to HTTPS**.

verification.description: Secret secret-tls is made from the provided certificate and key
Ingress rocket-ingress routes rocket-server.local to rocket-server:80 with TLS from secret-tls
https://rocket-server.local is served by the application
The controller serves the provided certificate for rocket-server.local
HTTP requests for rocket-server.local are redirected to HTTPS

questions.question:
The worker node `{{NODE01}}` (`ssh {{NODE01}}`) runs a Docker-style daemon as the systemd service `dockerd-lab`. It has no Docker Engine: this service accepts the same settings as `dockerd`: the flags `-H`/`--host` and `--group` in the unit, or `hosts` and `group` in `/etc/dockerd-lab/daemon.json` (the same setting in both places makes the daemon refuse to start).

Currently the daemon is bound to an external TCP port and its socket is not owned by the root group. Harden it:

1. The daemon must run under the **root group**.
2. **No external TCP connections** may be allowed to the daemon (it keeps its local unix socket `/run/dockerd-lab.sock`).
3. The configuration must be **persistent** across restarts of the service.

verification.description: The daemon runs with the group root (its socket belongs to root)
The daemon accepts no TCP connections and keeps its unix socket
After a restart of the service the group is root and there is no TCP listener

questions.question:
A security audit flagged the worker node `{{NODE02}}` (`ssh {{NODE02}}`) for ICMP redirects on the interfaces that will be created from now on (the `default` settings): the node accepts and sends them.

Disable both, `net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects` and `net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects`:

- immediately, on the running kernel;
- persistently, so that the settings survive a reboot of the node.

verification.description: net.ipv4.conf.default.accept_redirects is 0 on the running kernel
net.ipv4.conf.default.send_redirects is 0 on the running kernel
accept_redirects = 0 survives a reboot (sysctl files applied again)
send_redirects = 0 survives a reboot (sysctl files applied again)

questions.question:
The cluster administrator wants a strict labelling policy for the namespaces of the laboratory. Create it with a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy**:

- Name of the policy: `require-env-label`; name of its binding: `require-env-label-binding` (the binding must deny the requests that violate the policy).
- Every **new Namespace whose name starts with `lab-`** must have the label `env` (the value does not matter, only the key).
- Namespaces whose name does not start with `lab-` must not be affected.

To test it, create namespaces named `lab-...` with and without the label (they are removed when the session ends).

verification.description: The policy require-env-label for namespaces and its binding (Deny) exist
A namespace lab-... without the label env is rejected
A namespace lab-... with the label env (any value) is accepted
Namespaces that do not start with lab- are not affected

questions.question:
A test Pod `test-falco` runs on the worker node `{{NODE01}}` in the namespace `devmem-lab` (Falco is installed on `{{NODE01}}`). Do not modify the Pod and do not create `/dev/mem` inside it.

Configure a custom Falco rule that detects attempts of a process **inside a container** to read `/dev/mem`:

1. Add the rule to `/etc/falco/falco_rules.local.yaml` on `{{NODE01}}`; the rule is named `devmem`.
2. The detection must work even though `/dev/mem` does not exist in the container and the read therefore fails.
3. The priority of the rule is `NOTICE`.
4. The output of the alert is exactly `Shell (container_id=<container_id>)`, where `<container_id>` is the id of the container that triggered the event.
5. The rules file must be valid (Falco must load it together with the default rules).

How the condition is written and how lists or macros are named is up to you. You can test with `kubectl exec -n devmem-lab test-falco -- cat /dev/mem`.

verification.description: The local rules file is valid, loads with the default rules and defines devmem
The rule devmem fires when the container tries to read /dev/mem
The priority of devmem is NOTICE
The output is Shell (container_id=<id of the container>)
The test Pod is unchanged and has no /dev/mem
Only the app=backend Pods of web-tier reach the database Pods on 3306; the others are denied
The allowed backend reaches TCP 3306 only, not 8080
The database Pods can only send DNS (UDP and TCP 53) to the cluster DNS Pods
The env=dev Pods reach the Kubernetes API server over HTTPS
A Cilium policy allows env=dev Pods to reach the entity kube-apiserver

questions.question:
The directory `/tmp/exam/mhagou-007-q11/` has the binaries `kubelet`, `kube-proxy`, `kubeadm` and `kubectl` in `bin/`, and a reference file `reference.sha512` (SHA-512 checksums in the `sha512sum` format, paths relative to that directory).

Verify the integrity of the binaries against the reference file and **delete the binaries that do not match**. The binaries that match must be kept as they are.

verification.description: The binaries that do not match the reference are deleted
The binaries that match the reference are kept untouched
